summary: Francis Brinkley was a scholar of Japanology. He studied at the Royal School Dungannon and held a post at the University of Tokyo from around 1878 to 1886.

Francis Buchanan-Hamilton worked in history and archaeology. He earned an MD at the University of Edinburgh studying under John Hope, later serving in the Bengal and Indian Medical Services, at the East India Company, and directing the Indian Botanic Garden.

Francis Gladwin worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and Indology. He was a founding member of The Asiatic Society (~1784–1812) and served as a professor of Persian at Fort William College (~1801–1805).

Francis Harold Cook was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison. He served as Professor (~1970–1987) and Emeritus Professor at UC Riverside and chaired the Numata Center and Bukkyo Dendo Kyokai.

Francis N. J. is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Calicut, completing a Master's in Ancient History and doctoral research under the supervision of M. R. Raghava Varier (attested 2002).

Francis Vincent Tiso is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. Educated at Cornell, Harvard, Columbia, and Union Theological Seminary, he has held posts at Columbia, Sapienza University of Rome, and the Pontifical Gregorian University.

Francis Wilford worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He served as a fellow member of The Asiatic Society (~1784–1822) and was Secretary to the committee at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1799–1822).

Francis William Bain was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Westminster School and Christ Church, Oxford, before serving as Professor of History and Political Economy at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (~1892–1919).

Francis Woodman Cleaves was a scholar in Sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied at Dartmouth, at Harvard, and under Paul Pelliot, later serving as a professor at Harvard University from 1941 to 1980.

Francis X. Clooney specializes in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. After studying at Fordham and the University of Chicago, he held posts at Boston College, the University of Oxford, the Oxford Centre for Hindu Studies, and Harvard University.
Francisco García Ayuso was a scholar in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Munich (~1872–1874) under Martin Haug.

Francisco Varela worked in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and neuroscience. Educated at the Pontifical Catholic University of Chile, University of Chile, and Harvard under Torsten Nils Wiesel and Humberto Maturana, he held positions at CNRS, Pitié-Salpêtrière Hospital, and École Polytechnique.

Franciscus Verellen specializes in Sinology and religious studies. Educated at the University of Hamburg, University of Oxford, and EPHE under Kristofer Schipper, he taught at EPHE and Columbia before serving as Director of the École française d'Extrême-Orient (1991–2021).

Frank E. Reynolds was a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. He spent his career at the University of Chicago, serving as Professor from around 1972 to 2000 and as Professor Emeritus from around 2000 to 2019.
Frank F. Conlon is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Minnesota (1969) and later served as Professor Emeritus at the University of Washington (~2006).

Frank J. Hoffman is a scholar in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa and under Stewart Sutherland, Eliot Deutsch, David J. Kalupahana, Prithwish Neogy, Rama Nath Sharma, and Kashi Nath Upadhyaya.

Frank J. Korom is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. He was a graduate student at the University of Pennsylvania (attested 1990) and later served as a Professor at Boston University (attested 2005).

Frank Lee Woodward worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Sidney Sussex College and under Caroline Rhys Davids, and he held posts as Dean of Mahinda College (1903–1919) and translator for the Pali Text Society (~1919).

Frank Raymond Allchin specialized in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at SOAS under K. de B. Codrington, later serving as Lecturer at SOAS (1954–1959) and Lecturer and Reader in Indian Studies at the University of Cambridge (1959–1989).

Frank-Richard Hamm was a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his doctorate at the University of Hamburg under Walther Schubring, teaching there from 1948 to 1964 before becoming a Professor at the University of Bonn in 1965.
